principle: Generate fixed, orthogonal, PIT-safe candidate mechanisms without performance ranking or tuning.

candidates.mechanism: Abnormal security-level short-sale volume ratio followed by next-session return test.
candidates.fixed_measure: 20-trading-day standardized short-sale-volume share, computed only from completed FINRA daily files.
candidates.pit: FINRA daily file public by <=18:00 ET on trade date; action no earlier than next eligible session.

candidates.mechanism: Short-volume shock conditioned on contemporaneous price reaction, separating possible informed pressure from liquidity provision.
candidates.fixed_measure: Short-volume z-score crossed with same-day market-adjusted return sign.
candidates.pit: Same as I1A; updated files must preserve original-versus-updated provenance.

candidates.mechanism: Open-market insider purchase breadth: count of distinct reporting owners purchasing in the same issuer within a fixed window.
candidates.fixed_measure: 10-calendar-day cluster breadth after EDGAR acceptance timestamp.
candidates.pit: Use acceptance datetime; trade/report date never substitutes for public availability.

candidates.mechanism: Open-market insider purchase dollar imbalance, excluding grants, exercises, gifts and administrative transactions by fixed transaction-code rules.
candidates.fixed_measure: Net open-market purchase value divided by prior reported shares outstanding, accumulated over 20 calendar days.
candidates.pit: Next eligible trading session after final qualifying filing acceptance.

candidates.mechanism: First-revision macro surprise: revision between first available observation and next vintage.
candidates.fixed_measure: Fixed vintage-to-vintage change in a predeclared single series; exact series IDs frozen before coverage.
candidates.pit: Vintage date is the information cutoff; no later revised observation may enter the signal.

candidates.mechanism: Extreme trader-position crowding change in a fixed futures contract mapped to a predeclared equity/sector proxy.
candidates.fixed_measure: Weekly standardized change in non-commercial net position.
candidates.pit: Use actual public-release date, not report date; publication interruptions become explicit missing states.

candidates.mechanism: Abnormal firm-attention shock from Wikipedia pageviews.
candidates.fixed_measure: Completed-day pageview count relative to a fixed trailing baseline, with immutable issuer-to-page mapping.
candidates.pit: Only complete daily observations; next-session action; API lag explicitly recorded.

candidates.mechanism: Abnormal media negativity/attention shock at issuer level.
candidates.fixed_measure: Fixed-source-set z-score of daily article tone and article count from archived GDELT exports.
candidates.pit: Archive filename/checksum and article timestamps are immutable inputs; entity resolution frozen.

candidates.mechanism: Insider-purchase confirmation when contemporaneous public attention remains normal or low, designed to separate informed flow from attention-chasing.
candidates.fixed_measure: I2A purchase breadth intersected with I5A attention state; both mappings fixed before coverage.
candidates.pit: Each source has its own public-availability cutoff; usable signal is only after both cutoffs pass.

candidates.mechanism: Short-sale shock versus insider-purchase shock disagreement as a latent information-conflict state.
candidates.fixed_measure: Sign disagreement between I1A and I2A after independent PIT certification.
candidates.pit: Intersection of the independently certified next-session cutoffs; no same-day retroactive alignment.

literature_basis.supports: Short-selling activity can contain information about future abnormal returns.
Open-market insider purchases are the more informative insider transaction class in classic evidence.
Vintage-aware data revisions contain information relevant to asset pricing.
Trader-position sentiment and crowding can relate to subsequent futures returns/volatility.
Changes in Wikipedia pageviews have been studied as investor-attention measures.

literature_basis.source: Media-tone literature including recent GDELT work
literature_basis.supports: Media tone/attention can contain cross-sectional or firm-level return information.
